newsitem.title: FINLAND: Neste/Statoil's Borealis ups NSP stake to 100 pct.
newsitem.headline: Neste/Statoil's Borealis ups NSP stake to 100 pct.

text.p: Polyolefins maker Borealis A/S said in a statement on Wednesday it had agreed with Montell Polyolefins to buy Montell's 50-percent stake in North Sea Petrochemicals NV (NSP), upping its stake to 100 percent.
Borealis is 50/50 owned by Finnish energy group Neste Oy and Norwegian Statoil A/S.
Montell is a 50/50 joint venture between Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Italy's Montedison SpA.
"Borealis and Montell ... have signed an agreement for Borealis to acquire Montell's 50 percent share of (NSP) ... making Borealis the sole owner," Borealis said.
Borealis would continue to supply up to half of NSP's output to Montell until January 1, 2000, it said.
NSP operates a 250,000 tonnes per year polypropylene plant in Kallo, Belgium, Borealis said.
It said another company, NSP Olefins NV, would remain 50/50 owned by itself and Montell.
Borealis said its takeover of NSP was "an important milestone for Borealis in positioning ourselves as one of the leading polypropylene suppliers to the European market".
The deal would also serve to reinforce its role as a leading global polyolefin company, Borealis added.
